correctness.rationale: The standard Type-A pairwise criterion identifies graph edges with unique alternating phase toggles over the first-to-last differing interval. An interval pair yields another graph edge only if it shares one endpoint with free ends separated by at least two, or forms two adjacent disjoint intervals with an equal-symbol join and common unordered symbol pair. Pairwise constraints force one common-endpoint pencil, or two pencils straddling an equal-symbol boundary; the latter intervals cannot bridge that boundary because it would break alternation. The one/two-pencil free-endpoint packing gives at most floor(n/2) neighbors in a clique, and toggling even-length prefixes of a binary alternating base word attains floor(n/2)+1 for every q>=2. Independently enumerated all one-deletion balls and computed max cliques for (q,n)=(2,2),(2,4),(2,6),(3,4), agreeing with theorem; these finite tests are not its infinite proof.
